name: Rice Kheer
description: Traditional creamy Pakistani rice pudding slowly cooked with milk, basmati rice, cardamom and nuts.
ingredients: ¼ cup basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20–30 minutes
½ cup sugar, or to taste
method: Drain the soaked rice. Bring the milk to a gentle boil in a heavy-bottomed pot, stirring so it does not catch.
Add the rice and cardamom, reduce the heat and simmer gently, stirring regularly, until the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced.
Lightly mash some of the softened rice against the side of the pot to give the kheer a naturally creamy texture.
Add the sugar only after the rice is tender. Continue cooking over low heat until the sugar dissolves and the kheer reaches a creamy consistency.
Stir in most of the almonds and pistachios and cook for another 2–3 minutes. Add rose water after turning off the heat if using.
Serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate until chilled. Garnish with the remaining nuts.
tips: Use a heavy pot and stir frequently, especially near the end, because milk can scorch easily.
Kheer thickens further as it cools, so stop cooking while it is slightly looser than your final desired consistency.
storage: Cool promptly, cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Keep chilled until serving.
